description: Panel object returned by {@link window.GetPanel} or {@link window.GetPanelByIndex}

name: Move
signature: Move(x, y, width, height, repaintParent = false)

name: ButtonObject
description: Button object returned by {@link window.CreateButton}

name: Click
description: Assigns click handler function. See also global callback 'on_button_click'

name: PerformanceEntry
description: Performance timeline entry created by {@link performance.mark performance.mark} or {@link performance.measure performance.measure}.

properties.name: entryType
properties.description: Entry type. JSplitter currently supports "mark" and "measure".

properties.name: name
properties.description: User-defined entry name.

properties.name: startTime
properties.description: Start timestamp in milliseconds relative to {@link performance.timeOrigin}.

properties.name: duration
properties.description: Entry duration in milliseconds. Always 0 for marks; for measures it is endTime - startTime and may be negative.

properties.name: detail
properties.description:
Optional metadata associated with the entry. Defaults to null.
JSplitter note: unlike the Web User Timing specification, detail is currently retained as the original JavaScript value and is not structured-cloned.

name: PerformanceMarkOptions
description: Options accepted by {@link performance.mark performance.mark}.

properties.name: detail
properties.description:
Arbitrary metadata associated with the mark.
JSplitter note: the value is not structured-cloned.

properties.name: startTime
properties.description: Finite non-negative timestamp in milliseconds relative to {@link performance.timeOrigin}. Defaults to {@link performance.now performance.now}.

name: PerformanceMeasureOptions
description: Options accepted by the standard options form of {@link performance.measure performance.measure}.

properties.name: detail
properties.description:
Arbitrary metadata associated with the measure.
JSplitter note: the value is not structured-cloned.

properties.name: start
properties.description: Start mark name or finite non-negative timestamp in milliseconds.

properties.name: duration
properties.description: Finite non-negative duration in milliseconds. May be used together with start or end, but not together with both.

properties.name: end
properties.description: End mark name or finite non-negative timestamp in milliseconds.

name: PerformanceObserverOptions
description: Options accepted by {@link PerformanceObserver.observe PerformanceObserver.observe}.

properties.name: entryTypes
properties.description: Entry types to observe. Unsupported types are ignored. Use either entryTypes or type for an observer, not both.

properties.name: type
properties.description: A single entry type to observe. Unsupported types are ignored. Use either type or entryTypes for an observer, not both.

name: PerformanceObserverCallback
description: Callback invoked when observed performance entries are delivered.

name: PerformanceObserverEntryList
description:
List of performance entries delivered to a {@link PerformanceObserver PerformanceObserver} callback.
The entries in this list are ordered by {@link PerformanceEntry.startTime startTime}.

name: getEntries
description: Returns all entries in this callback's entry list, ordered by {@link PerformanceEntry.startTime startTime}.

name: getEntriesByType
description: Returns entries in this callback's entry list filtered by entry type and ordered by {@link PerformanceEntry.startTime startTime}.

name: getEntriesByName
description: Returns entries in this callback's entry list filtered by name and, optionally, entry type. Results are ordered by {@link PerformanceEntry.startTime startTime}.

params.name: type
params.description: Optional entry type, for example "mark" or "measure".

name: PerformanceObserver
description:
Creates a new observer for entries added to the JSplitter performance timeline.
The callback is invoked asynchronously when {@link performance.mark performance.mark} or {@link performance.measure performance.measure} records an entry whose type is currently observed. Entries created in the same event-loop burst may be delivered together in one callback.
JSplitter currently supports only the "mark" and "measure" entry types. The Web Performance Timeline buffered option is not implemented.

params.name: callback
params.description: Callback invoked when matching entries are delivered.

name: supportedEntryTypes
description:
JSplitter compatibility alias for the standard static {@link PerformanceObserver.supportedEntryTypes PerformanceObserver.supportedEntryTypes} property.
Returns the same frozen array object as the static property.

name: observe
description:
Registers performance entry types to observe.
Use either entryTypes or type for a given observer until {@link PerformanceObserver.disconnect disconnect} is called. Switching between the two modes throws an error.
Repeated calls using the same mode add supported types to the observer's current set. Unsupported entry types are ignored.
JSplitter currently supports only entryTypes and type; the Web Performance Timeline buffered option is not implemented.

throws.description: If options is not an object or if the observer switches between entryTypes and type modes without first calling {@link PerformanceObserver.disconnect disconnect}.

name: disconnect
description:
Stops delivery of future performance entries, clears pending observer records, and resets the observer's registered entry types.
The same observer may be configured again with {@link PerformanceObserver.observe observe} after disconnecting.

name: takeRecords
description:
Returns the performance entries currently waiting in the observer buffer and empties that buffer.
Entries returned by this method will not later be delivered by the callback.

name: unknown@168
description:
Frozen array of entry types supported by {@link PerformanceObserver PerformanceObserver}.
JSplitter currently returns ["mark", "measure"]. Repeated reads return the same frozen array object.

name: performance
description:
High-resolution timing API implementing the JSplitter subset of the Web High Resolution Time, User Timing, and Performance Timeline APIs.
JSplitter currently records only user-created "mark" and "measure" entries; browser-specific navigation, resource, paint, and similar performance entry types are not available.
For the corresponding Web standards, see {@link https://www.w3.org/TR/hr-time-2/ High Resolution Time}, {@link https://www.w3.org/TR/user-timing/ User Timing}, and {@link https://www.w3.org/TR/performance-timeline/ Performance Timeline}.

name: now
description:
Returns a monotonically increasing high-resolution timestamp in milliseconds relative to {@link performance.timeOrigin}. The value may contain a fractional part; actual resolution depends on the underlying system clock.
Unlike Date.now(), this timestamp is intended for measuring elapsed time and is not affected by wall-clock adjustments.

name: mark
description:
Creates a named {@link PerformanceEntry} with entryType "mark" and adds it to the performance timeline.
Multiple marks may use the same name. All marks remain in the timeline until cleared; when a mark name is later used by {@link performance.measure performance.measure}, the most recently created matching mark is used.

returns.description: The created mark entry.

throws.description: If startTime is not a finite non-negative number.

name: measure
description:
Creates a named {@link PerformanceEntry} with entryType "measure" and adds it to the performance timeline.
Standard forms supported by JSplitter:
performance.measure(name) - measures from timestamp 0 to {@link performance.now performance.now}.
performance.measure(name, startMark) - measures from the most recent named start mark to now.
performance.measure(name, startMark, endMark) - measures between the most recent matching named marks.
performance.measure(name, options) - derives start/end times from {@link PerformanceMeasureOptions}.
performance.measure(name, {}, endMark) - measures from timestamp 0 to the named end mark.
In options, start and end may be either mark names or finite non-negative timestamps. duration may be supplied with exactly one of start or end. If an explicitly named mark does not exist, an error is thrown.
Multiple measures may use the same name. Named mark lookup always uses the most recently created matching mark.
Compatibility note: for historical JSplitter compatibility, a fourth legacyMeasureOptions argument is also accepted. This form preserves the previous JSplitter precedence rules: existing explicit startMark/endMark values take precedence, while numeric start, end, or duration options fill missing values. New code should prefer the standard forms above.
For backward compatibility, an empty positional mark name ("") is treated as omitted rather than as a mark named with an empty string.

params.name: startOrMeasureOptions
params.description: Start mark name or standard measure options.

params.name: legacyMeasureOptions
params.description: JSplitter legacy four-argument options object. Supports numeric start, end, duration, and arbitrary detail.

returns.description: The created measure entry.

throws.description: If a named mark cannot be resolved, a numeric timestamp/duration is invalid, or the standard options contain an invalid combination.

name: getEntries
description: Returns all {@link PerformanceEntry} objects currently stored in the performance timeline, ordered by {@link PerformanceEntry.startTime startTime}.

name: getEntriesByType
description: Returns timeline entries filtered by entry type and ordered by {@link PerformanceEntry.startTime startTime}.

name: getEntriesByName
description: Returns timeline entries filtered by name and, optionally, entry type. Results are ordered by {@link PerformanceEntry.startTime startTime}.

params.name: type
params.description: Optional entry type, for example "mark" or "measure".

name: clearMarks
description:
Removes mark entries from the performance timeline.
If name is supplied, all marks with that name are removed. If omitted, all mark entries are removed. Clearing a mark also removes it from subsequent named-mark lookup by {@link performance.measure performance.measure}.

name: clearMeasures
description:
Removes measure entries from the performance timeline.
If name is supplied, all measures with that name are removed. If omitted, all measure entries are removed.

name: toString
description: JSplitter extension that returns a human-readable dump of the current performance timeline.

name: Observer
description:
JSplitter compatibility factory that creates a {@link PerformanceObserver PerformanceObserver}.
New code may use the standard new PerformanceObserver(callback) form instead.

params.name: callback
params.description: Callback invoked when matching entries are delivered.

name: timeOrigin
description:
Read-only Unix timestamp in milliseconds corresponding to the origin used by this performance timeline.
{@link performance.now performance.now} values are measured relative to this origin.

name: WorkerMessageCallback
description: Callback used for Worker message and messageerror handlers.

name: WorkerErrorCallback
description: Callback used for Worker error handlers.

name: WorkerPromiseRejectionCallback
description: Callback used for Worker Promise rejection handlers.

name: Worker

params.name: source
params.description: JavaScript source text, or a file descriptor object such as { file: 'workers/main.js' }.

params.name: name
params.description: Optional immutable Worker identity exposed through read-only Worker-global {@link WorkerGlobalScope#name name}, reported by {@link window.JsMemoryStats}, and shown in unhandled Worker exception diagnostics.

throws.description: If the arguments are invalid, a file-backed Worker cannot resolve or read its startup file, or the Worker cannot be created or started.

name: RunAsync
description:
Runs a user-defined JavaScript callback once in a temporary Worker and returns a Promise for its result.
A fresh full Worker realm/thread is created for every call. Arguments are structured-cloned into the Worker; a synchronous return value or the resolved value of an asynchronous callback is structured-cloned back. The temporary Worker is terminated automatically when the operation settles.
The callback is recreated from its source and does not capture lexical variables from the caller. Pass required values explicitly through args. Native and bound functions are not supported. Relative {@link include include()} calls keep the caller's script/package roots.
This API does not currently expose a transfer list. For repeated requests, persistent Worker state, or explicit ownership transfer, use a normal {@link Worker} and {@link Worker#postMessage postMessage()}.

params.name: callback
params.description: User-defined JavaScript function to execute in the temporary Worker. The function may return a value or a Promise.

params.name: args
params.description: Values passed to callback through structured clone.

returns.description: Promise resolved with the structured-cloned callback result. It rejects if the callback throws or rejects, the callback cannot be recreated, Worker startup fails, or an argument/result cannot be structured-cloned.

throws.description: If callback is not callable or the RunAsync helper itself cannot be initialized.

name: onmessage
description: Receives messages sent from the Worker through Worker-global {@link WorkerGlobalScope#postMessage postMessage()}.

name: onerror
description:
Receives uncaught Worker errors reported to the parent endpoint as an {@link ErrorEvent}.
The callback argument exposes the error text through {@link ErrorEvent#message message} and the original Worker source location through {@link ErrorEvent#filename filename}, {@link ErrorEvent#lineno lineno} and {@link ErrorEvent#colno colno}.
If no parent error handler exists, the Worker error is promoted to the normal panel-script error UI/failure path. Throwing from this handler likewise propagates as a normal panel script exception, whose stack begins in the parent handler.

name: onmessageerror
description: Receives a {@link MessageEvent} when a serialized message cannot be reconstructed by the parent endpoint. {@link MessageEvent#errorMessage errorMessage} contains the reconstruction failure and {@link MessageEvent#direction direction} is worker-to-panel.

name: postMessage
description: Serializes and sends a value to the Worker. Sender-side serialization and transfer-list validation are synchronous; successful delivery to the Worker is asynchronous.

params.name: transfer
params.description: Transfer list, either directly as an array or as an object containing { transfer: [...] }.

throws.description: If the required data argument is omitted, the value cannot be structured-cloned, or the transfer list is invalid or cannot be committed. No message is queued and transferable source objects remain usable when this happens.

name: terminate
description:
Stops this Worker from the parent panel and releases pending Worker-side state.
Use this when the panel no longer needs the Worker; Workers are terminated automatically when their parent panel is unloaded.
A main-thread host callback that has already begun executing cannot be interrupted halfway through.

name: EventTarget
description: Base event target used by Worker objects, Worker global scopes and {@link BroadcastChannel} objects.

name: addEventListener
description: Registers an event listener.

params.name: callback
params.description: Function or object with a handleEvent() method.

name: removeEventListener
description: Removes a matching event listener.

name: dispatchEvent
description: Dispatches an event to registered listeners.

returns.description: false when a cancelable event was canceled, otherwise true.

name: Event
description: Standard-style event object used by the Worker event system.

name: type
description: Event type supplied when the event was created, for example message or error.

name: target
description: Event target on which the event was originally dispatched. It is null before dispatch.

name: currentTarget
description: Event target whose listener is currently being invoked. It is null outside listener dispatch.

name: defaultPrevented
description: true when {@link Event#preventDefault preventDefault()} successfully canceled the event's default action.

name: cancelable
description: Whether {@link Event#preventDefault preventDefault()} can cancel this event.

name: bubbles
description: Whether the event participates in bubbling through an event-target hierarchy.

name: MessageEvent
description: Event carrying a structured-clone message payload. Used by direct Worker messaging and {@link BroadcastChannel} in both panel and Worker realms.

name: data
description: Structured-clone payload carried by a message event.

name: origin
description: Message origin. JSplitter Worker and BroadcastChannel messages use an empty string because they are not URL-origin messages.

name: lastEventId
description: Last event identifier. JSplitter Worker messages do not use event-stream IDs, so this is an empty string.

name: source
description: Message source endpoint. JSplitter Worker and BroadcastChannel messages do not expose a MessagePort-style source, so this is null.

name: ports
description: Transferred message ports. JSplitter does not expose MessagePort objects, so this array is empty. Trusted JSplitter messaging events expose it as an empty frozen array.

name: errorMessage
description: JSplitter reconstruction diagnostic for a messageerror event. It contains the structured-clone read failure reported by the receiving endpoint and is an empty string for an ordinary message event.

name: direction
description: Direction of a JSplitter message: panel-to-worker, worker-to-panel, or broadcast for {@link BroadcastChannel}. Manually constructed MessageEvent objects use an empty string unless a direction is supplied explicitly.

name: ErrorEvent
description: Event carrying an uncaught Worker error. Trusted Worker error events dispatched by JSplitter are non-cancelable because handler presence itself determines whether the error is handled.

name: message
description: Human-readable error message reported by the failing Worker script or callback.

name: filename
description: Script filename associated with the error when one is available. File-backed Workers report the basename, matching panel-script diagnostics.

name: lineno
description: One-based source line associated with the error, or 0 when unavailable.

name: colno
description: Source column associated with the error, or 0 when unavailable.

name: error
description: Original thrown JavaScript value when it can be exposed to the receiving realm.

name: PromiseRejectionEvent
description: Event used for unhandled and later-handled Worker Promise rejections.

name: promise
description: Promise whose rejection triggered this event.

name: reason
description: Rejection reason associated with {@link PromiseRejectionEvent#promise promise}.

name: WorkerGlobalScope
description: Global object available inside every JSplitter Worker.

name: self
description: The Worker global object itself.

name: name
description: Immutable Worker identity supplied through the Worker constructor. The value is fixed for the Worker's lifetime. JSplitter reports the same name in {@link window.JsMemoryStats} and in unhandled Worker exception diagnostics. If no name was supplied this value is an empty string; diagnostics display it as <unnamed>.

name: postMessage
description: Serializes and sends a value from the Worker to its parent. Sender-side serialization and transfer-list validation are synchronous; successful delivery to the parent is asynchronous.

params.name: transfer
params.description: Transfer list, either directly as an array or as an object containing { transfer: [...] }.

throws.description: If the required data argument is omitted, the value cannot be structured-cloned, or the transfer list is invalid or cannot be committed. No message is queued and transferable source objects remain usable when this happens.

name: close
description:
Requests Worker shutdown from inside the Worker after the current task completes.
Use this when Worker code itself knows that no more event-loop work is needed.

name: onmessage
description: Receives messages sent by the parent through {@link Worker#postMessage Worker.postMessage()}.

name: onmessageerror
description: Receives a {@link MessageEvent} when a serialized parent message cannot be reconstructed by the Worker. {@link MessageEvent#errorMessage errorMessage} contains the reconstruction failure and {@link MessageEvent#direction direction} is panel-to-worker.

name: onerror
description: Global error handler for uncaught Worker task exceptions. The callback receives an {@link ErrorEvent} with the error text and Worker source location. When this handler or a Worker-global error listener is installed, the error is handled locally and is not forwarded to the parent Worker.

name: onunhandledrejection
description: Handler for newly unhandled Promise rejections.

name: onrejectionhandled
description: Handler for Promise rejections that later become handled.

name: performance
description: Worker-local performance timeline.
